newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Debt vols better bid but unfazed by Iraq.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Debt vols better bid but unfazed by Iraq.

text.p: European debt options were unfazed by news of a U.S. military strike on Iraq on Tuesday, but the market on the whole was better bid, traders said.

A report in the Wall Street which said Federal Reserve policy makers were considering a half percentage point rate rise this month had more impact and with all markets suffering, vols were slightly firmer.

Mark Bays, broker at Mees Pierson Derivatives, said one of the notable features in the market was out-of-the-money put buying in October Bunds. "Really apart from that I think the options trade been a little lacklustre," he said.

Analysts said comments from Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing on Monday were seen in the market as signalling a likely trough for short-term rates and this was contributing to the downward bias in the underlying market.
"We have created clarity for the foreseeable future," Issing said.
Dealers said October Bund volatility was quoted around 4.95 percent, up slightly from 4.85 on Monday. LIFFE data show October 96.50 strike options finishing around 4.66 percent on Monday.
"There have been put buyers overall but I wouldn't be buying puts in October," Bays said.
At the short end, Euromarks and other European interest rate contracts were also bid but there were no dramatic moves.
A dealer at a U.S. bank in London said that Euromark volatility was firmer but nowhere near the levels before the August German repo cut.
"We came off for a good week. We've now stabilised and gone a little bit bid," the trader said.
The trader said December Euromarks vols were around 15.25 percent, up from a recent 14.1 percent low but down from around 20 percent before the repo cut.
